User Journey

You might say

Map the whole experience from first hearing about the product to actually using it, including where people get stuck.

A staged view of a user's actions, thoughts, feelings, and obstacles across touchpoints while pursuing a goal·A learner might discover a course through a friend, visit its page, pay, receive an email, and enter the first lesson. A user journey needs interview or behavioral evidence and must not present team assumptions as real feelings.
Know first
User Flow
User Journey MapCustomer JourneyCustomer Journey Map
Follow a learner from discovery to the first lesson
TouchpointFriend share
User actionOpen course page
FeelingCurious
EvidenceInterview and behavior notes

The journey connects touchpoints across time and keeps evidence attached to each claim.

How a user journey represents the complete experience

Start with one user and goal: Define the user, situation, and time span instead of mixing different people's experiences.

Connect touchpoints inside and outside the product: Social sharing, pages, payment, email, the app, and support may all affect one goal.

Separate evidence from assumptions: Interviews, feedback, and behavior data support claims; team guesses remain hypotheses.

What people often confuse

A User Journey spans time and touchpoints with actions, thoughts, feelings, and evidence. A User Flow focuses on pages, actions, and decisions for one in-product goal.

You can say this to an AI Agent

“

Map the user journey for buying and starting a course for the first time across discovery, evaluation, purchase, notification, and first learning. For each stage, state the touchpoint, action, question, feeling, obstacle, and available evidence. Label interview quotes separately from behavioral data and mark unsupported claims as hypotheses. Identify the friction that needs more research without reducing the journey to an in-product user flow.
